title: Separate ink components by paper chromatography
subject: chemistry

steps.instruction: Mark a pencil line 2 cm from the bottom of the chromatography paper.
Apply a small dot of ink on the pencil line.
Place the inked paper into the solvent jar so the dot is just above the solvent level.
Observe the separated colors as the solvent travels up the paper.

rules.feedback: The paper is ready for marking with a pencil line 2 cm from the bottom.
A small ink dot is applied at the marked spot.
The solvent travels up the paper by capillary action, separating the ink components.
Watch as the solvent travels and separates the ink colors into distinct bands.

outcomes.title: Colors separated
outcomes.description: The solvent has traveled up the paper, carrying different ink pigments at different rates, creating distinct colored bands.

safeFailure.message: Paper chromatography separates colors by solubility.
safeFailure.guidance: Place the paper so the ink dot is just above the solvent level. Watch carefully as colors separate.

narration.text: Take a pencil and mark a line 2 cm from the bottom of the chromatography paper. Use pencil, not pen, so the marking doesn't dissolve.
Using a small brush or cotton swab, apply a small dot of ink on the marked line. The dot should be small and distinct.
Place the inked paper into the solvent jar so the ink dot is just above the solvent level. Don't let the paper touch the solvent.
Watch as the solvent travels up the paper. Different pigments travel at different rates, separating into distinct colored bands.

captions.text: Mark a pencil line 2 cm from the bottom of the chromatography paper.
Apply a small ink dot on the marked line using a brush.
Place the paper in the solvent jar. The solvent rises by capillary action.
Observe the separated colored bands as the solvent travels up the paper.
